standard_prerequisites.name: Surjection onto a module from a direct sum of extensions by zero
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Modules on Sites, the lemma representing a sheaf of modules as a quotient of a direct sum of j_{U!} of the structure sheaf over affine objects
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the surjection onto the kernel of K^b -> K^{b+1} used at the start.

standard_prerequisites.name: Constructible sheaves are finitely generated over the colimit
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma stating that a constructible sheaf is the union of the images of maps from finitely many extension sheaves
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the image of a finite sub-sum already equals H^b(K).

core_obligations: Project the kernel onto the cohomology sheaf (proof lines 13622-13628): represent K by a complex K^bullet and use the surjection Ker(K^b -> K^{b+1}) -> H^b(K).

Choose a surjection from extension sheaves (proof lines 13629-13634): by the modules-on-sites lemma there is a surjection from the direct sum over a set I of j_{U_i!}Lambda with U_i affine onto the kernel.

Cut down to a finite sub-sum (proof lines 13635-13641): for finite subsets I' the images H_{I'} of the corresponding sub-sums form a directed family whose union is H^b(K), so constructibility gives H_{I'} = H^b(K) for some finite I'; taking F as that finite sum and composing gives the required map F[-b] -> K inducing a surjection on H^b.
proof_roadmap: Write H^b(K) as a quotient of the kernel of the differential.
Surject from a direct sum of extensions by zero over affine objects onto that kernel.
Use constructibility to pass to a finite sub-sum whose image is all of H^b(K).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a finite sum of extension-by-zero sheaves mapping to a given complex and surjecting onto its constructible cohomology sheaf in degree b (statement lines 13610-13619). The proof (proof lines 13621-13641) uses the modules-on-sites representation of the kernel of the differential as a quotient of a direct sum of extension sheaves, and then cuts down to a finite sub-sum using constructibility of H^b(K). H2: one representation plus one finiteness step, written out.
